findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.153 - Pan of cheese on make line in ice bath had surface and internal temperatures of 58F and 46F respectively. Employee stated time control is being used, and the cheese in question was out/in-use for approximately 1hr. Employee did not document the time anywhere in the work area. Cheese from the 2 door cooler was added the pan, and that cheese had an internal temperature of 50F (see below). All cheese in the pan was discarded. New pan was placed on make line with cheese from the walkin cooler (37F-40F).

Track the time for products that are being time controlled. All foods that are out of temperature and do not have time documented at future inspections will be discarded if time control is being used. When using time as a control, food must be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.
findings.citation_text:

The bag of cheese observed with an internal temperature of 46F was moved to the walkin cooler. The bag of cheese with an internal temperature of 57F was discarded in the trash. Staff and management noted the cheese was moved from the walkin cooler this morning and was not removed otherwise. All other products in the cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 40F/below. (see general comments)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Diced tomatoes and shredded cheese on make line had surface temperatures of 53F/54F (tomatoes) and 60F (cheese). Internal temperatures for products were 37F/39F (tomatoes) and 49F-53F (cheese). Foods were placed out in iced holding area around 9a. Ice was not surrounding all sides of containers. More ice was added to the holding compartments. All products would be used or discarded by 1p. Use of time control for cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) on the make line was discussed with Store Manager. Also, staff were advised pans of lettuce do not have to be on ice, and other products that don't require cold holding for safety reasons could be repositioned to allow for better cold storage in iced compartments for pans of cheese and containers of tomatoes (bottom and all sides of containers to be surrounded by ice).

Cold PHF shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, unless a time control is used. If facility wishes to use time control, then a policy must be established. Time would have to be tracked for working supplies of PHF, and foods would have to be used or discarded w/in 4hrs. Foods can not go back in the cooler once they are out for use and foods can not be kept for use past 4hrs if time control is used (time control policy sheet provided).

Maintain cold PHF at 42F/below or establish and adhere to a time control policy for working supplies of foods.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 (x2) - A) Refried beans in steam table had internal temperature range of 118F-157F. Beans were pulled from the walkin cooler and reheated in the microwave w/in the last hour. Internal temperature of the beans was not checked by employee prior to placing product in the steam table.  Manager placed beans in microwave to finish reheating to 165F. Manager verified proper reheat temperature with a stem thermometer prior to placing beans back in the steam table for hot holding. 
B) Tamales in hot holding steam well with soft shells had internal temperatures of 116F-125F. Manager noted the tamales went directly from the cooler to the hot holding steam well at 9:30a. Temperatures were checked in the two o'clock hour. All tamales were discarded in the trash. Manager stated heating tamales in the microwave causes issues with quality of the product. Manager was advised to try using the cookie oven to heat prior to being placed in the steam well and/or leave tamales in the cooler and heat to order. Manager is immediately changing the current practice and will figure out new procedure for tamales.
Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout. The only way to know a food has reached proper temperature is to use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to verify cooking/reheating temperatures. Always reheat foods to 165F using microwave and other equipment intended for such purposes (i.e. kettle cookers, fryer, etc.) prior to placing foods in the steam table and other hot holding areas. The steam table and steam well of the table are intended to hold foods at 135F/above after products have been properly reheated using other equipment intended for reheating. Properly reheat foods to 165F/above.
